gitCommit.subject: Stop the candidate specs deadlocking on their own interceptor
gitCommit.body:
Stop the candidate specs deadlocking on their own interceptor

interceptSubmit is async and returned the pending request promise directly.
An async function that returns a bare promise unwraps it, so
`await interceptSubmit(page)` waited for a request that only the lines after
that call could trigger. Both specs hung until the 90s timeout with no
assertion error to point at, because nothing had actually failed.

Returning the promise inside an object keeps it unresolved across the await.

Verified by breaking the code under test: with dismissSelected reverted to
collecting every checkbox, "discarding sends only the ticked row" fails; with
it restored, all six pass. That check was worth running twice — the first
attempt passed against a stale bundle, since development serves precompiled
public/assets and yarn build alone never reaches the browser.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
